name: SpatialViz-Bench
ability_definition: The ability to imagine how something will look after it is moved around or when its parts are moved or rearranged.

task_realism.reasoning: The tasks are mental rotation, paper and cube folding, cross-sections and projections, and mechanical animation. These are the operations Visualization requires, and they resemble the psychometric tests used to define the ability. However, they are abstract puzzles on synthetic shapes. Real workplace tasks involve domain objects in context, such as reading blueprints, planning an assembly, fitting parts, or picturing surgical anatomy.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation is static and zero-shot, with single images and no tools, iteration, physical manipulation or consequences. Workers usually can sketch, rotate a CAD model, test-fit parts or ask for clarification. Programmatic generation reduces contamination, and the text-only chance baseline confirms the images are actually needed. Still, the input distribution is clean, idealized renders rather than messy real-world visuals.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers four cognitively grounded sub-abilities across 12 tasks: rotation, folding, penetration/cross-section, and animation of moving parts. This spans most of the O*NET definition of imagining objects after they are moved or rearranged. It is weaker on open-ended rearrangement and assembly planning, on large-scale or real-object transformations, and on generating a visualization rather than recognizing one.

format_match.reasoning: Answers are forced-choice from about four options on synthetic diagrams. Real work produces decisions, sketches, assembly sequences or fit judgments on technical drawings, photos or physical objects. Recognizing the correct option is easier than, and different from, constructing the answer.

transferability_reasoning: SpatialViz-Bench is a well-designed, contamination-resistant measure of the core mental operations behind Visualization, with good coverage of its cognitive sub-components. Its transfer to workplace capability is limited by abstract psychometric-style stimuli, static zero-shot conditions and a multiple-choice format that do not resemble real visual-spatial work artifacts or workflows.

2025.metric: accuracy (%) on multiple-choice questions, averaged over all 1,180 items
2025.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: adults who routinely do spatial visualization work, such as technicians, drafters and engineering-adjacent workers. The published human baseline (82.46%) most likely comes from educated adult participants.

2026.human_reference: General adult / educated workforce performing everyday spatial visualization at work, such as technicians, trades workers, drafters and assemblers. Psychometric-style mental rotation, paper folding and cube-net tasks are standard aptitude items for this population.
